Why it matters · in the research, not just my run

“…dazzling back-tested returns evaporate once the model’s knowledge window ends.”

Li et al., Profit Mirage: Revisiting Information Leakage in LLM-based Financial Agents, arXiv 2510.07920, Oct 2025 · grade A

Also: Sarkar & Vafa, SSRN 4754678 (2024) · Levy, Chicago Booth, SSRN 5082861 (2024) · Zhang et al., arXiv 2602.17234 (2026): the fix needs time-filtered retrieval.

        Appendix

        Method, sources, objections, caveats.

        Method and sources · 1 of 4

        The fence and fintech numbers.

        data/fintech_judged.json
        33/60 results state the outcome unfenced; 0/60 acquired after the cutoff with query_time; 1/60 later text; primary source in top 10 on 14/40.
        data/h2h/latest_judged.json
        A publish-date fence on the same engine: 29/70 results still state the outcome.
        data/fence_relevance.json
        Useful pre-event results per top 10 on 7 events: 0.4 no fence, 0.6 publish-date, 4.3 query_time (raw Jev labels; 6/70 flagged as possible leaks, 1 confirmed).

        Method and sources · 2 of 4

        Labels, replays and load.

        data/fence_gold.json
        30 results labelled blind by a second model (Claude); Jev agreed on 28/30. No human validation yet.
        data/fintech_repro.json
        The same fenced request, run twice: identical order on 6/6 queries.
        data/fintech_stress.json
        Open-loop ramp 0.5 to 2 rps: 300/300 requests OK.

        Method and sources · 3 of 4

        Coverage, latency, build vs buy.

        data/cc_overlap.json
        75.4% [71.4–79.0] of 500 Keenable-returned pages have no URL match in any of the nine 2026 Common Crawl crawls.
        data/needle_results.json
        NEEDLE: Finance recall@5 0.886, #3 by rank; median p95 pro 1,336 ms, realtime 169 ms.
        data/charts/opt1_montecarlo.json
        Galactica build vs buy over ranged inputs, 10,000 draws: build cheaper in 0 of them.

        Objections → answers · 1 of 2

        Six objections I expect, answered.

        "We already use Exa or Tavily."
        Their date filters fence on publish date; on Keenable's engine that still leaked 29/70.
        "Is query_time today's copy of an old URL?"
        0/60 acquired after the cutoff, but 1/60 served later text. Proposed fix: versioned snapshots.
        "You rank aggregators first."
        True on finance: primary source in top 10 on 14/40. site: plus fetch today.

        Objections → answers · 2 of 2

        Crawl, cost and latency, answered.

        "Common Crawl is free."
        75.4% of 500 sampled pages have no URL match in a 2026 crawl. The gap is coverage.
        "We already crawl."
        Existing-team low scenario: ~$0.86M a year. Sell Delta, priced per novel document.
        "Latency at our RPS?"
        300/300 OK to 2 rps keyless. 100 RPS gets a contracted load test in the pilot.

        Full lists: opt2_thesis.md §6 · opt1_thesis.md §8

        Caveats · 1 of 2

        What these numbers do not prove.

        n = 7 events
        The fence result covers seven market events. A pilot runs 200 of the buyer's.
        Keyless endpoint
        Every call went through /v1/search/public. There, pro and realtime returned identical lists.
        Residential latency
        Client-side from a San Francisco Mac, last mile included. Not a server SLO.

        Caveats · 2 of 2

        Still unproven: rivals at scale, forecasts, labels.

        One rival run
        Seven rivals ran once on 1 Oct, free tiers, 7 events and up to 40 queries, snippets only. Small n; see the head-to-head.
        Monte Carlo
        A bounds argument over ranged inputs, not a forecast.
        Jev labels
        Checked against a second model (Claude) on 30 fence results: 28/30. No human validation yet.
